therapeutic_hypothesis.intended_biology: photoprotective behavior adoption and skin cancer risk reduction
therapeutic_hypothesis.target_population: families with children at risk for melanoma

results.target_engagement_evidence: Demonstrated improvements in multiple photoprotective behaviors including sunscreen use, protective clothing, and shade-seeking
biomarker_changes: Reduced UV exposure measured by dosimeter (-1.38 J/m²)
Decreased melanin index in children indicating less tanning
Reduced unprotected sun exposure minutes via PALE questionnaire
subgroup_findings: Parents showed sustained improvements in long-sleeve shirt wearing and long pants/skirt wearing
Children demonstrated improvements in protective clothing behaviors
Both parents and children increased skin self-examination thoroughness
